The [starter](../../starters/nucleo-f767zi.md) scaffolded a C talker for
`board = "nucleo-f767zi-zephyr"`, ran it in the board's Renode twin over the
serial link, and flashed the same image to an ST Nucleo-F767ZI. This page
covers what comes after it: the image's link and RAM budget, what is
particular to the board and its twin, and what the board does not do yet.
Zephyr's own configuration (`system.toml` against `prj.conf`, one image per
RMW, driving `west`) is the same on every Zephyr board; the
[Zephyr native_sim](zephyr-native-sim.md) page covers it.

## Configure the platform

The starter's image reaches the router over USART3, the UART the board's
ST-LINK carries to your USB port as a virtual COM port:

```toml
[image.zephyr]
board = "nucleo-f767zi-zephyr"
locator = "serial/serial@40004800#baudrate=115200"
```

`serial@40004800` is Zephyr's devicetree name for USART3. The board's own
configuration turns Zephyr's IP stack off for this image and gives USART3 to
zenoh, so the serial image needs no `prj.conf` of yours. In the twin,
`nros run` connects USART3 to a terminal device on your host and starts the
router on it; on the board, `nros flash --monitor` starts the router on the
ST-LINK's USB serial device instead.

### Fit an image in the board's RAM

The STM32F767ZI has 384 KiB of main SRAM, and nano-ros's default pools do
not fit it. The board's descriptor states the one setting every image on
this RAM needs, and each image inherits it:

```toml
# the board's descriptor, inherited by every image
[knobs.zenoh]
max_large_subscribers = 0
```

An image that needs a different budget states the knob itself, and the
image wins:

```toml
[image.zephyr.knobs.zenoh]
max_subscribers = 2
```

Never set these in `prj.conf`: a `CONFIG_NROS_*` line there is a configure
error. [Measure static memory](../contracts/measure-static-memory.md) reads
an image's boot report, so you can see how much room a change leaves.

## Board notes

- **STM32F767ZI, a Cortex-M7 with a double-precision FPU,** 2 MiB of flash,
  384 KiB of main SRAM and 128 KiB of DTCM, on Zephyr 3.7. The west
  workspace needs Zephyr's `hal_stm32` module, and
  `nros setup board nucleo-f767zi-zephyr --zephyr-workspace <ws>` applies
  nano-ros's patches to it and adds the `thumbv7em-none-eabi` Rust target.
  The image is soft-float: Zephyr's board configuration leaves `CONFIG_FPU`
  off.
- **The twin boots the same ELF.** Renode's `nucleo_f767zi` machine runs the
  image you flash, with USART3 on a host terminal device. A twin result
  predicts the board result for the parts the twin models.
- **The console is USART6,** on the Arduino header's D0 and D1 pins, so the
  ST-LINK cable carries only the zenoh link. Reading the console on the bench
  takes a USB-to-UART adapter on those pins.
- **Flashing is Zephyr's own runner for the board,** OpenOCD over the
  ST-LINK. [Flash a real board](flash-a-real-board.md) covers `nros flash`,
  `nros monitor` and naming the port.
- **The status above is a dated manual check.** Someone booted the image in
  the twin by hand on that date. After the registry's stale period the word
  reads *Builds* until someone boots it again.

## Ethernet is not set up yet

The board's on-chip ethernet MAC works in the twin with Zephyr's
`eth_stm32_hal` driver: an early run reached a router over `tcp/`. That run
needed a host tap device bridged to Renode's virtual switch, which takes
`CAP_NET_ADMIN`, and `nros run` does not set one up. An ethernet image also
needs Zephyr's IP stack back on and a tighter RAM budget than the serial
image, and its boot report is not yet measured, so neither the starter nor
this page documents one. Use the serial link. WiFi is not available on this
board.

## If it doesn't work

- **The twin boots and the router never hears the board:** the image's
  `locator` names another UART. It must be USART3,
  `serial@40004800`.
- **The build stops on RAM:** an image knob raised a pool past the board's
  budget. Lower it, or remove the image's override.
- **On the bench, nothing on the console:** the console is USART6 on the
  header pins, not the USB cable.
- **Everything else:** [Troubleshoot](../deploy/troubleshoot.md).
